Know

What is Community?

Understand the PMM supporting role in community engagement — and how product expertise activates advocates.

Overview

What this area is

Community is the practice of engaging SAP product communities, user groups, and advocacy networks to amplify awareness, build peer credibility, and sustain loyalty. PMM does not own community strategy — that sits with Customer Success, Developer Relations, and Events — but it owns the product messaging and expertise that communities rely on to stay informed and willing to advocate.

Responsibilities

What this PMM area is accountable for doing.

  • Support the community strategy with product expertise and content
  • Provide briefings to community moderators and advocates
  • Identify and activate product advocates
  • Develop community content including FAQs and product update summaries

Needs PMM validation

Key deliverables

The artifacts and outputs PMM is expected to produce.

  • Community content briefs
  • Advocate activation playbook
  • Community product FAQ library
  • Product update summaries for community audiences

Needs PMM validation

Collaborators & interlocks

Who you work with and what each interlock requires.

  • Customer Success → advocate identification and community health
  • Developer Relations → technical community engagement
  • Product → product update content and roadmap signals
  • Marketing → community events and programmes

Needs PMM validation

Inputs required

What you need before you can execute this work well.

  • Community feedback themes from moderation teams
  • Advocate nominations from Customer Success
  • Product update announcements from Product
  • Community engagement metrics

Needs PMM validation

Playbook
1

Map community touchpoints

Identify the key communities, forums, user groups, and events where product voice creates the most value. Prioritise by audience size and advocacy influence.

2

Identify advocate candidates

Work with Customer Success to surface customers who are already championing your product in their networks. Qualify by enthusiasm, expertise, and reach.

3

Develop community content

Create product update briefs, FAQs, and talking points that are accessible to community audiences — not just internal field teams.

4

Activate advocates

Onboard advocates with product context, messaging, and narrative. Facilitate peer storytelling without scripting — authenticity is the value advocates bring.

5

Measure community influence

Track advocate activity volume, community engagement rates, and the proportion of pipeline sourced from community-engaged accounts.

KPIs
Engagement
Community engagement rate
Average interaction rate (posts, replies, likes, shares) across product community touchpoints per quarter.
Program
Advocate program size
Number of active, briefed product advocates enrolled in the advocacy program at end of quarter.
Loyalty
NPS from community members
Net Promoter Score among community participants compared to the overall customer NPS baseline.
Pipeline
Community-influenced pipeline
% of total pipeline from accounts where a community touchpoint or advocate interaction was recorded.

AI Workflows In development

End-to-end tasks you run to accomplish a specific goal — provide context, get a structured output.

Community Content Ideator

Input recent product updates, community feedback themes, and advocacy goals. Get a structured content plan with angle recommendations by audience segment.

Advocate Profile Builder

Paste customer success data and community activity. Get a scored list of high-potential advocate candidates with recommended activation approaches.

Community Feedback Synthesizer

Input community discussion data or moderation notes. Get a structured synthesis of product feedback themes for PMM and Product review.
